To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the plant in LLD PE was more eco-friendly, even comparing each phase of the life-cycle and for all the assessed treatment capacities, and that the results were not dependent of the impact assessment method.
the plant in LLDP was always more eco-friendly than the plant in VRC, for all the impact assessment methods and for the whole range of capacities.
the construction phase was the most impacting one for the LLDPE plant and the use phase for the VRC plant.

the comparison of two small-scale wastewater treatment systems, both based on an activated sludge process.
the environmental assessment of two different small-scale wastewater treatment plants.
a new approach to the LCA of wastewater treatment plants, which is based on the comparison of different materials and technologies.

the plant in LLD PE has the best performance and the plant in (VRC) has the worst one, for all the treatment capacity values and the three impact assessment methods considered in this work.
, for the considered case study, the LLDPE system was always less impactful, even when compared to each single phase of its life cycle.
the use phase of a small-scale treatment plant in concrete is more impactful than the use phase of the same plant in LLDPPE, even if the construction phase of the plant in concrete is less impactful.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the plant made of LLDPE is more environmentally friendly than the one in VRC, and this is valid for all the considered phases of the life cycle, for the different treatment capacities, and for the three different impact methods.
the plant in LLD PE was more eco-friendly in terms of the environmental impacts than the plant in VRC.
the plant in LLDP was more eco-friendly and the plant in VRC more impactful than the plant in LDDPE.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the environmental impacts of the use phase of the treatment systems in LLDPE and VRC were always higher than those of the construction phase, which is in contrast to what is commonly assumed in the literature.
the construction phase is the most important one for small-scale treatment systems, which is not true for large-scale systems.

the environmental impacts of on-site small-scale treatment plants are dominated by the operation phase, and therefore, the use of energy efficient equipment and low-impact chemicals are the most effective ways to reduce the impacts.
